title: Current lags voltage in an inductor
back: Inductor: current peaks a quarter cycle after voltage. Capacitor: current leads by π/2.

title: Phasor diagram of series LCR
back: V_R along I, V_L up, V_C down; V = √(V_R² + (V_L − V_C)²); tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R.

title: Resonance curve
back: Peak at ω₀ = 1/√(LC); smaller R gives a taller, sharper peak.

title: AC generator
back: Coil turning at ω in B: Φ = NBA cos ωt, emf = NBAω sin ωt; slip rings and brushes take it out.

title: Transformer
back: Mutual induction on a laminated soft-iron core: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p = I_p/I_s. AC only.

title: rms values
back: Meters and "220 V mains" are rms; the peak is about 311 V.

title: Inductive and capacitive reactance
back: X_L ∝ ν; X_C ∝ 1/ν. A capacitor blocks DC.

title: Impedance of series LCR
back: I = V/Z. At resonance Z = R.

title: Resonant frequency
back: Current is maximum and in phase with the voltage.

title: Average power and power factor
back: Pure L or C: cos φ = 0, wattless current.

title: AC generator emf
back: Largest when the plane of the coil is parallel to B.

title: Ideal transformer
back: High-voltage transmission keeps the current, and so I²R loss, small.

title: Who leads in L and in C?
back: "ELI the ICE man": in L, E (voltage) before I; in C, I before E. The lead or lag is always π/2.
